findings.title: The authenticated GitHub user is not verified when the installation record has not arrived yet
findings.body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises, this branch immediately advances the pipeline and creates the integration without comparing the OAuth-authenticated user to the installation webhook sender. Webhook delivery is asynchronous, so this is a normal window after an app installation (or whenever a webhook was missed). A user can complete OAuth for their own GitHub account and substitute a known victim installation ID in the callback/request during that window, causing that installation to be associated with the attacker's Sentry organization. The flow must not accept a new installation ID until it has trusted installer identity data to compare, or must obtain an authoritative installer identity before advancing.

findings.title: Optional sender metadata can crash the installation pipeline
findings.body: `build_integration` only adds `metadata['sender']` when pipeline state contains a sender, so sender is explicitly optional (and existing integrations may also predate sender storage). On the existing-Integration/no-OrganizationIntegration path, indexing `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` raises `KeyError` or `TypeError` instead of returning the intended failed-installation response. This can occur after an organization association is removed while its Integration remains, leaving users with a 500 and preventing recovery. Treat absent or malformed sender metadata as an invalid installation request.
